newsitem.title: JORDAN: King Hussein releases Jordan's leading dissident.
newsitem.headline: King Hussein releases Jordan's leading dissident.

text.p: King Hussein of Jordan ordered the release on Friday of a leading opposition figure who was jailed in March for branding the monarch a traitor for making peace with Israel, state television reported.

Laith Shubailat, head of the Islamist-dominated engineers union and a vocal critic of Jordan's 1994 peace treaty with Israel, was jailed on charges of violating the king's dignity after a series of scathing public attacks on his policies.
The king said in a letter to Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti that Shubailat's eight months behind bars were enough punishment.
"This letter stands as our decree from the moment of your receiving it to order the release of engineer Laith Shubailat," said the king's letter, read out on state television.
Family members said Shubailat was released from Suwaqa prison south of Amman shortly before the decree was announced.
"God knows that the period Shubailat spent in prison weighed heavily on my soul as it was on him and his family, and I, thank God, am not one who bears grudges," said the king's letter.
"God forgives what is past and leads us all to the paths of goodness, reform, and piety of speech and work," it said.
Shubailat, a former parliamentary deputy, was sentenced to death in 1992 for attempting to overthrow the government, but was pardoned in the same year.
"I am happy for his release," Shubailat's wife Rima told Reuters. "But I am angry that others are still there," she said in reference to detainees imprisoned on similar charges of insulting the king.
Human rights groups accuse the government of exploiting laws curbing criticism of the monarch to make widespread arrests. The government has denied the allegations.
Shubailat was arrested in December after a speech branding the king a traitor by citing the Hashemite dynasty's links with the Zionist movement before the creation of Israel in 1948.
In March he was sentenced to three years in jail for violating the dignity of the king, his American-born wife Queen Noor and Crown Prince Hassan, and distributing inflammatory leaflets.
The judge who sentenced him, Mohammed Faleh al-Shara, said a series of public speeches given by Shuabailat last year showed he had abused freedom of expression.
"His Majesty the king cannot be in a position of accountability," Shara said at the sentencing in March.
Jordan's peace treaty with Israel has disappointed most Jordanians, who expected quick economic benefits from ending the 46-year state of war with Israel.

King Hussein, seen as the Arab leader with the warmest ties with Israel, distanced himself from the Jewish state after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu opened a tunnel near Moslem holy sites in Jerusalem, where Jordan has custodial rights.
Netanyahu's decision, taken in September without consultation with Jordan or the Palestinians, sparked violence in the West Bank and Gaza Strip in which 75 people were killed.
